plan.summary: This 1-4 block is the opening building phase for an off-camp 12-week boxing strength and power plan. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the main percentage-based lifts with one assessment lift per session, then Weeks 2-4 build force and power with short, high-value sessions that fit around boxing work. Review bar speed, soreness, and boxing fatigue at the end of Week 4 before the next block is set.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Establish training maxes, build general strength, and keep explosive work present without adding unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main lifts and power work while keeping weekly fatigue controlled around boxing training.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Turn the earlier strength gains into faster, sharper power and speed without forcing a fight-camp peak.

exercises.name: 1a. Box Jump
exercises.notes: Low box, soft landing, reset between reps. Jump fast and stop if height drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if boxes are busy or setup is limited. Keep each rep crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a simple low-impact option. Pause briefly before takeoff.

exercises.name: 2. Back Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up progressively, then work to one hard top set with clean depth and no grindy form. This session establishes your baseline for future percentage work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your squat max for later weeks.

substitutionOptions.name: Safety Bar Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if the shoulders or wrists do not like the back rack.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if squat patterning is cleaner here and depth is easier to control.

exercises.name: 3a. Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Drive the elbows back and keep the chest glued to the pad. Stop with 1-2 reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if no row bench is available. Keep the torso stable.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you need a simple, easy-to-coach row.

exercises.name: 3b. Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.notes: Brace hard, reach long, and stop before the lower back extends.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Rollout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if no ab wheel is available.

substitutionOptions.name: Cable Crunch
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if rollout quality is not good today.

exercises.name: 1a. Medicine Ball Chest Pass
exercises.notes: Use a non-bouncing or low-bouncing throw. Throw every rep fast from the chest and reset fully between efforts.

substitutionOptions.name: Plyo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if no med ball or wall space is available. Keep reps snappy and low.

exercises.name: 2. Bench Press
exercises.notes: Warm up progressively, then work to one hard top set with full control and a brief pause on the chest if that keeps the rep honest. This session establishes your baseline for future percentage work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your bench max for later weeks.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if barbell setup is crowded or shoulders prefer dumbbells.

substitutionOptions.name: Swiss Bar Bench Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if a neutral grip feels better on the shoulders.

exercises.name: 3a. Pull-Up

substitutionOptions.name: Lat Pulldown
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if clean pull-up reps are not there today.

substitutionOptions.name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up

exercises.name: 3b. Half-Kneeling Cable Lift

substitutionOptions.name: Pallof Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if cable setup is limited.

exercises.name: 1a. Rotational Medicine Ball Scoop Throw

substitutionOptions.name: Rotational Medicine Ball Shot Put

exercises.name: 2. Trap Bar Deadlift
exercises.notes: Warm up progressively, then work to one hard top set with a flat back and clean lockout. This session establishes your baseline for future percentage work.
